evidence_kind: synthetic forward-test fixtures, not observed website state

findings.observation: Canonical homepage returns 302 to preview; destination HTML has robots noindex and canonical back to the redirecting origin.
findings.impact: Public organic landing path ends at an excluded preview URL. Canonical and robots Allow do not cancel noindex.
findings.action: Confirm public-launch intent. When launch is authorized, serve meaningful indexable content at the canonical production URL; keep preview exclusion according to owner policy and align canonical signals.
findings.confidence: high for capture; live state unverified
findings.validation: Fresh unauthenticated GET records every redirect hop. Production URL serves intended 200 HTML with correct self canonical and no exclusion in meta or X-Robots-Tag. Keep preview policy deliberate. Owner GSC URL Inspection checks selected canonical and indexing after crawl.

findings.observation: The only supplied sitemap loc is the preview homepage, which carries noindex in the saved HTML.
findings.impact: Sitemap advertises a URL outside the declared canonical host and excludes the desired production landing URLs.
findings.action: After host policy is settled, list only intended canonical indexable production URLs. Include /ansible only after verifying its canonical response and policy.
findings.confidence: high for capture; sitemap coverage beyond fixture unknown
findings.validation: Parse fresh XML; every listed URL has the approved production host, intended 200 response, matching canonical and no noindex. Check sitemap processing in GSC.

findings.observation: Three-row GSC sample lacks property ID, retrieval time, search type, completeness and indexing data. No NL rows. Bing/Ahrefs unavailable; Semrush access expired.
findings.impact: Cannot assess market totals, trends, complete indexing or current provider rankings. Small sample can guide investigation only.
findings.action: Use owner-verified GSC read access or repeatable exports with property, period, search type, filters and coverage. Keep country and device slices for BE/DE/NL and indexing separately; retain first-party data independently of Semrush.
findings.validation: Saved export metadata identifies property and filters, row/completeness limits and retrieval time. Country coverage explicitly distinguishes no rows from zero traffic; repeat matched periods.

findings.observation: Saved HTML has title Automation, H1 Automation for your team, one Ansible link and no meta description or signup/contact/install link. It includes unrelated instruction text.
findings.impact: The supplied page gives little context about audience, capabilities or the next step. Full production and rendered experiences remain untested.
findings.action: At the intended public landing page, explain the product and audience with concrete supported details; use a descriptive title/summary and a clear next step. Remove unrelated page text. Review rendered journeys before concluding site-wide quality.
findings.confidence: high for saved HTML; medium for user impact
findings.validation: Inspect initial and rendered public HTML, visible copy and title. Follow a clear task path through the main product page to the intended conversion without credentials until access control.

findings.observation: Relative /ansible link resolves on the preview host; GSC sample refers to production /ansible. Neither URL has supplied response/content evidence.
findings.impact: Visitors and crawlers may follow a different host from the page recorded in GSC. No broken-link or noindex conclusion is established for /ansible.
findings.action: Check both targets and intended host behavior after canonical routing is resolved; assess the real Ansible page before planning new content.
findings.confidence: high for URL resolution; outcome unknown
findings.validation: Bounded fresh read of both authorized URLs records redirects, status, canonical, exclusion directives, meaningful initial/rendered content and onward links.
findings.period: capture and GSC sample use different periods

findings.observation: Sample includes ansible controller in BE desktop (3 clicks/80 impressions) and DE mobile (1/20), plus opentofu automation in BE desktop (0/12). English is the supplied content language; NL evidence is absent.
findings.impact: Existing query-page pairs offer a starting point for intent research, without proving country demand or a localization business case.
findings.action: First inspect whether /ansible answers controller evaluation and practical adoption questions using real product evidence. Check OpenTofu intent and homepage fit. Validate German/Dutch and Belgian language needs before translating or adding pages; avoid duplicate pages solely for countries.
findings.validation: Review actual page content and country/language query evidence, then compare like property/period/device slices. Measure relevant impressions, clicks and intended conversions after authorized changes without promising lift.
